title: Stable influence and Boolean influence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\\{−1,1\\}^n\\to\\{−1,1\\}$ be a Boolean function. For each coordinate $i$, the square of the stable influence of its real-valued version at parameter $1/3$ is at most the cube of its Boolean influence, where Boolean influence is the uniform probability that flipping coordinate $i$ changes the value of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean-valued function on the sign cube
